questions.question: What is the stereochemical relationship of the two methyl groups in the product of catalytic hydrogenation of 1,2-dimethylcyclopentene over Pt?

options.label: C
options.text: cis-1,2-dimethylcyclopentane exclusively (meso compound), because both hydrogens are delivered simultaneously to the same face of the planar alkene from the metal surface.

questions.correct_answer: cis-1,2-dimethylcyclopentane exclusively (meso compound), because both hydrogens are delivered simultaneously to the same face of the planar alkene from the metal surface.
questions.explanation: Heterogeneous catalytic hydrogenation delivers two hydrogens from the catalyst surface in a stereospecific syn addition.

questions.question: Why does the bromination of cyclohexene yield trans-1,2-dibromocyclohexane rather than the cis isomer?

options.label: A
options.text: Bromination proceeds via a bridged cyclic bromonium ion; bromide must attack from the opposite (backside) face, enforcing anti stereochemistry.

options.label: B
options.text: Bromine atoms are too large to fit on opposite sides.

options.label: D
options.text: The cis isomer is an explosive compound.

questions.correct_answer: Bromination proceeds via a bridged cyclic bromonium ion; bromide must attack from the opposite (backside) face, enforcing anti stereochemistry.
questions.explanation: Backside opening of the 3-membered cyclic bromonium intermediate dictates strict anti stereospecificity.

questions.question: What is the stereochemical outcome when 1-methylcyclohexene is subjected to hydroboration-oxidation (1. BH₃·THF, 2. H₂O₂/NaOH)?

options.label: A
options.text: trans-2-methylcyclohexanol (racemic), resulting from concerted syn-addition of H and B followed by oxidation with complete retention of configuration.

questions.correct_answer: trans-2-methylcyclohexanol (racemic), resulting from concerted syn-addition of H and B followed by oxidation with complete retention of configuration.
questions.explanation: Syn addition of H-BH₂ followed by alkaline peroxide oxidation with retention delivers H and OH syn, yielding trans-2-methylcyclohexanol.

questions.question: When cis-2-butene is treated with mCPBA, what is the stereochemical structure of the resulting epoxide?

options.label: C
options.text: cis-2,3-dimethyloxirane (meso-epoxide with an internal plane of symmetry), preserving the cis orientation of methyl groups.

questions.correct_answer: cis-2,3-dimethyloxirane (meso-epoxide with an internal plane of symmetry), preserving the cis orientation of methyl groups.
questions.explanation: Peroxy acid epoxidation is a concerted syn-addition that strictly preserves the stereochemical relationship of alkene substituents.

questions.question: What is the stereochemical relationship between the -Br and -OH groups in the bromohydrin of 1-methylcyclopentene?

options.label: B
options.text: trans-2-bromo-1-methylcyclopentanol: the -OH and -Br groups are strictly trans (anti addition), with -OH located at the more substituted C1 carbon.

questions.correct_answer: trans-2-bromo-1-methylcyclopentanol: the -OH and -Br groups are strictly trans (anti addition), with -OH located at the more substituted C1 carbon.
questions.explanation: Water attacks the more substituted carbon of the cyclic bromonium ion from the backside, enforcing anti stereochemistry and Markovnikov regiochemistry.

questions.question: What is the stereochemical outcome of treating trans-2-butene with OsO₄ / NMO?
questions.correct_answer: (±)-(2R,3R)/(2S,3S)-butane-2,3-diol (a racemic pair of chiral enantiomers).
questions.explanation: Syn addition of two hydroxyl groups across a trans alkene produces a racemic mixture of chiral (R,R) and (S,S) enantiomers.

questions.question: What is the stereochemical outcome of treating cis-2-butene with OsO₄ / NMO?

options.label: D
options.text: meso-butane-2,3-diol (an optically inactive meso compound with an internal mirror plane).

questions.correct_answer: meso-butane-2,3-diol (an optically inactive meso compound with an internal mirror plane).
questions.explanation: Syn addition of two hydroxyl groups across a cis alkene produces the symmetric meso diastereomer.

questions.question: What stereoisomer is formed when cis-2-butene is converted to an epoxide and opened with aqueous acid?

options.label: D
options.text: (±)-(2R,3R)/(2S,3S)-butane-2,3-diol (racemic diol), because the anti opening inverts one stereocenter of the cis framework.

questions.correct_answer: (±)-(2R,3R)/(2S,3S)-butane-2,3-diol (racemic diol), because the anti opening inverts one stereocenter of the cis framework.
questions.explanation: Anti-dihydroxylation of cis-2-butene yields the racemic chiral pair of enantiomers.

questions.question: What stereoisomer is formed when trans-2-butene is epoxidized with mCPBA and opened in aqueous acid?
questions.correct_answer: meso-butane-2,3-diol (optically inactive meso diol).
questions.explanation: Anti-dihydroxylation of trans-2-butene yields the symmetric meso diol.

questions.question: Why does reductive ozonolysis of (E)-3-methyl-2-pentene yield acetone and acetaldehyde with zero stereocenters remaining?

options.label: B
options.text: Ozone racemizes the alkyl chain by homolysis.

options.label: C
options.text: The stereocenters are inverted into (S) configurations.

options.label: D
options.text: Because oxidative cleavage of the double bond transforms both sp² alkene carbons into planar, achiral carbonyl groups (C=O).
